text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto says is more optimistic about a decrease in unemployment than ever during the government's term.
- Banks returned to the black with a total 1996 operating profit of 2.6 billion markka, excluding Interbank and Alandsbanken which have not yet reported 1996 earnings.
- Mortgage lending slowed at the end of last year on seasonal factors, banks expected growth in 1997. @
- Women have to be more flexible on the labour market than men, report shows.
- Helsinki council lifts leases for 50 houses despite protests from inhabitants.
- Privatisation likely for Postipankki within the next couple of years, CEO says.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Vocational education is being transferred to companies from the public sector, partly helped by EU money but tradition slows change, Minister of Education Olli-Pekka Heinonen says. @
- Merita's current capitalisation would enable it to increase lending by 75 billion markka, CEO Vesa Vainio says.
- Private Wihuri likely to merge its two airlines Jetflite and Euroflite.
- Finnish politicians' earnings rank seventh in the world compared to industry workers, World Economic Forum foundation study says.
AAMULEHTI
- Ministry of social affairs and health rejects idea of compulsory testing or isolating HIV-infected people to prevent the spread of AIDS. @
TURUN SANOMAT
- An average family can save up to 3,000 markka per year by following sales advertisments in newspapers.
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET
- Ex-mediator Jorma Reini, sacker earlier this year after he was sentenced for family violence, has been employed by a union to help firemen reach settlement in a prolonged conflict.

- Finnish Navy buys its first submarine since World War Two -- a tiny unmanned vessel built by Swedish Bofors -- after it unilaterally announced in 1991 it is no longer bound by the 1947 Paris Treaty's prohibition of Finnish submarines. @
